scenes.headline: How noisy points become clean Gaussians
scenes.sub: InfiniSplat v2, on top of a frozen Depth Anything 3
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mortise! Today: how a splatting model cleans a noisy point cloud without moving a single point.

scenes.text: Keep every point where the depth model put it, and let learned opacity fade the ones other views have seen straight through.
scenes.say: Leave the geometry alone. Every point stays where the depth model put it. The network only learns how visible each one is.

scenes.title: Two copies of one depth model

steps.say: The images go into a frozen copy of Depth Anything 3. It predicts depth and a camera for every view.
Back-project every pixel to get a point cloud. Good on average, noisy at every edge.
A second copy, with only its last ten blocks trained, feeds a small head: rotation, scale, opacity and colour, per pixel.
Centres come only from the depth. The head never outputs a position.

items.say: Divide by the average point distance, so a street and a table look alike.
Snap Gaussians to a grid and average each cell.
Delete anything nearly transparent. That is where the noise goes.

left.title: Learn offsets
left.say: The tempting fix is letting the network nudge points onto surfaces. In the paper's tests, renders got worse.

right.title: Fixed centres
right.say: Frozen positions leave the loss one way out: shape, colour and opacity.

steps.say: Labelled with true depth, inconsistent points pile up near zero opacity. Everything else sits near one.
So the threshold clears the mid-air haze and leaves the shelf alone.

scenes.label: of inconsistent points pruned, against 7.5% of all points
scenes.say: About half the inconsistent points vanish, and less than a tenth of everything.

scenes.title: Mean LPIPS with poses, lower is better
scenes.note: Six datasets; ReSplat keeps the higher PSNR
scenes.say: On perceptual error it leads clearly. On plain pixel accuracy, one baseline still edges it out.

scenes.text: Opacity can delete what sits in front of a surface. It cannot move a surface the depth model got wrong.
scenes.say: Opacity can delete what floats in front of a surface. It cannot move a surface the depth model got wrong.

recap: A trained branch predicts the rest
scenes.say: Frozen depth for position, learned attributes for the rest, and a threshold that cleans.
